M. iliofemoralis internus, status et forma generalis (ordered)  : present, fusiform (0);  present, short and broad (1);  absent (2).

M. flexor cruris lateralis (semitendinosus), pars pelvica, insertio, situs (unordered)  : m. gastrocnemius (pars intermedia aut medialis) et os tibia (0);  os tibia only (1);  m. gastrocnemius (pars intermedia aut medialis) only (2).
M. caudofemoralis, pars caudalis, status et forma (ordered)  : present, well developed (0);  present, poorly developed (1);  absent (2).
M. caudofemoralis, pars pelvica, status et forma (ordered)  : present, extremely large (0);  present, small to moderately large (1);  absent (2).
M. obturatorius medialis, origo, caput fossae renalis pelvici (new term), status  : absent (0);  present, typically prominent (1);  State 2 (2).
M. fibularis longus, status et forma (ordered)  : present, well developed (0);  present, poorly developed (1);  absent (2).

M. fibularis longus, origo, forma capitorum (unordered)  : both capita tibiale et fibulare (0);  caput fibulare only (1);  caput tibiale and underlying musculi (2);  noncomparable by absence of m. fibularis longus (see status) (3).
M. fibularis brevis, status et forma (ordered)  : present, well developed (0);  present, weakly developed (1);  absent (2).
M. gastrocnemius, origo tendinis m. femorotibialis intermedius (new term), status et forma (ordered)  : present, extensive (0);  present, moderate (1);  absent (2).
M. gastrocnemius, pars intermedia, status et forma (ordered)  : present, well developed (0);  present, weakly developed (1);  absent (2).
M. flexor perforatus digiti II, status (ordered)  : well developed (0);  vestigial (1);  absent (2).
M. flexor hallucis longus, tendo hallucis (new term), forma (ordered)  : absent (0);  rudimentary (1);  well developed (2).
M. flexor hallucis longus, numerus capitorum (ordered)  : one (0);  two (1);  three (2);  noncomparable by absence of musculus (ratites) (3).
M. flexor digitorum longus, corpus, forma (unordered)  : moderately developed, long (0);  distinctly enlarged, elongate (1);  extremely thick, truncate (2).

M. flexor digitorum longus, rami tendinis insertii, digiti insertiorum (unordered)  : digiti I--IV (0);  digiti II--IV (1);  digitus III (2);  noncomparable in absence or vestigial condition of digitus I et/aut II (3).
M. flexor hallucis brevis, status (ordered)  : present (0);  vestigial (1);  absent (2);  noncomparable in absence or vestigial condition of digitus I (3).
M. extensor brevis digiti IV, status (ordered)  : present, well developed (0);  present, vestigial (1);  absent (2).
M. adductor digiti II, status et forma (ordered)  : well developed (0);  vestigial (1);  absent (2);  noncomparable by absence of digitus II (Struthio) (3).
Projectio (crista) pennarum, status et forma (unordered)  : absent (0);  present, as crista of frons, corona et/aut occiput (1);  present, as floccus (new term) frontalis (2).

Rhinotheca et gnathotheca, tomia maxillare et mandibulare, lacinia oro-ocularis (new term), status et forma (ordered)  : absent (0);  present, abbreviate, typically extending approximately one-half of the distance between rictus et oculus (1);  present, extensive, typically extending virtually or wholly the distance between rictus et oculus (2).

Rhinotheca et gnathotheca, tomia maxillare et mandibulare, ungues maxillaris et mandibularis, lamellae rostri verae---typus anseriformis---status et forma (ordered)  : absent (0);  present, rudimentary (1);  present, well developed (2).

Rhinotheca, caudal (basal) extent relative to apertura nasalis, forma (unordered)  : limited to area within ovate or fissuriform spatium integumentum (0);  moderately extensive basally, but apertura nasalis enclosed within incisura of integument (cum pennarum) extending rostrad from regio facialis (1);  very extensive basally, apertura nasalis enclosed within rhamphotheca propria, i.e., rhinotheca extends caudad to form comparatively expansive lamina postnasalis rhinothecae (new term) between apertura nasalis and basis rhinothecae (2);  noncomparable through obfuscation by cera (Falconiformes sensu lato, Columbiformes sensu lato, Strigiformes) (3).

Rhinotheca, serratia maxillaro-tomiales rhinothecae (new term), status et forma (unordered)  : absent, tomia essentially linear or subtly, monotonically curved (0);  present, subserratia (new term), typically subtle, subtubercular (1);  present, serratia, typically extending majority of tomium (2).

Extremitas sternalis coracoidei, processus lateralis, status et forma (unordered)  : absent (0);  present, shallow, obtuse angulus (including rudimentary or vestigial), margo supraangularis linear (1);  present, tuberculum (variably oriented), width approximating length, margo supraangularis typically linear (2);  processus linearis, width markedly less than length, margo supraangularis linear (3);  processus hamularis, margo supraangularis curvilinear (4);  noncomparable (Aptornis) (5).

Extremitas sternalis coracoidei, facies ventralis, crista articularis sternalis, sectio medialis (new term), pila articularis columnaris externa (new term), status et labri (unordered)  : absent (0);  present, involving labrum externum only, but including both sectiones medialis et lateralis (1);  present, involving labrum externum, sectio medialis only (2);  present, involving labrum internum only (3);  present, involving both labri internum et externum (4);  present, involving both labri internum et externum, section ``intermedius'' or coincident with hiatus intersectionalis (5);  noncomparable (Aptornis) (6).

Junctura sternoclavicularis, involving extremitas sternalis claviculae and carina sterni, apex carina, status et typus (unordered)  : present, articulatio synovialis, facies articularis variably conformed (0);  present, elongate syndesmosis, attachment by comparatively elongate and ligamentum elasticus sternoclaviculare (1);  present, abbreviate syndesmosis, attachment by comparatively truncate and semikinetic ligamentum sternoclaviculare (2);  present, synchondrosis, deriving ontogenetically from junctura cartilaginis, typically retaining sutura vestigialis following ossification (3);  present, synostosis, sutura definitivum indiscernable (4);  absent, typically by absence of (conjoined) extremitas sternalis claviculae (5).

Junctura intercoracoidea et spatium intercoracoidale, status modalis et typus definitivum (ordered)  : absent---wide, symmetrical spatium intercoracoidale (0);  absent---close symmetrical, medial juxtaposition or virtually undifferentiable, extremely limited articulatio simplex (1);  present---an articulatio synovialis between extremitates sternales coracoidei, angulae (vertices) caudomediales, that of os coracoideum dexter ventral to that of os coracoideum sinister (2);  present---syndesmosis intercoracoideus or symphysis sternocoracoidea (3).

Canalis (foramen) omalis (triosseus), cranial composition, status, numerus et nomina ossae (unordered)  : absent (0);  present, biosseous, incomplete, involving ossa scapula et coracoideum (1);  present, triosseous, incomplete, involving ossa clavicula, scapula, et coracoideum (2);  present, triosseous, vestigial, involving limited margo claviculae vestigium (3);  present, uniosseous, involving only os coracoideum, restricted to taxa having arcus acrocoracoprocoracoideus (4).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, facies caudalis, incisura capitis humeri, laterodistal extension and orientation as sulcus incisurae transversus (new term), status et forma (unordered)  : absent (Dromaeosauridae [Velociraptorinae, Deinonychus], Enantiornis, Archaeopteryx, Confuciusornis) or obsolete by expansion of facies caudalis immediately distal to incisura (0);  absent, by obstruction related to fundamental alteration of underlying structure of extremitas proximalis humeri (1);  obsolete, by proximal continuity of caput et ventrally expanded crista deltopectoralis, associated with obsolescence and cranial shift of tuberculum dorsale (2);  present, separating caput humeri et tuberculum ventrale, terminating approximately at margo distalis capitus or persisting as broad sulcus to margo dorsalis fossae pneumotricipitalis without discern- able curvature (3);  present, separating caput humeri et tuberculum ventrale (``internus''), extending significantly toward or passing distad to tuberculum dorsale (other Neornithes, including in Galbula--``Passer'' [comparatively indistinct dorsal to margo caudalis corporis]) (4);  noncomparable by absence of ossa alae (Dinornithiformes, Aptornis) (5).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, facies (perspective) caudalis, incisura capitis humeri, forma generalis (unordered)  : absent or obsolete (0);  variably shallow, broad sulcus (1);  extremely narrow, constricted sulcus (2);  comparatively deep, subelliptical fossa (3);  noncomparable by absence of ossa alae (Dinornithiformes) (4).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, caput humeri, tuberculum dorsale (``externus''), forma (unordered)  : absent or indistinct (0);  present---impressio aut jugum, not elevated or buttressed, typically sloping distally with facies caudalis of corpus humeri (1);  present---tuberculum, prominent, buttressed, typically with facies articularis elevated, planar, and distinctly caudal to facies caudalis of corpus humeri (2);  present---tuberculum, diminutive, distinctly delimited by elevated rimae with central fovea, on facies cranialis of basis cristae (3);  present---facet, subelliptical, sloping with facies caudalis of crista deltopectoralis, distinctly outlined but caudal elevation obsolete (especially distally) and sometimes obscured in part by impressiones musculares (4);  diminished---small, proximal, indistinct, marginal facet (5);  obsolescent---minute irregularity approaching indiscernability (6);  noncomparable by absence, variable, unique form, or situs of element (ratites, Dromornithidae) (7).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, crista deltopectoralis (oblique caudal perspective), status et forma (profile) marginalis (unordered)  : absent or obsolete (0);  present, subarcuate (rounded-convex) and comparatively elongate, crista lacking distinct angulae (1);  present, essentially triangular, crista propria possessing one distinct angulus (2);  present, bi-tubercularly or bi-angularly concave, rudimenta evidently largely comprising two tuberculae separated by deep, arcuate concavity--- processus insertii m. pectoralis subcutanea thoracica (3);  secondarily diminutive, element practically acristate, often precluding reliable characterization of form (4);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) (5).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, crista deltopectoralis (oblique caudal perspective), proximodistal extent relative to that of crista bicipitalis, magnitudo (ordered)  : majority distal to latter (0);  substantial minority distal to latter (1);  slight or moderate minority distal to latter (2);  approximately equal to latter (3);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) or crista (Struthio, Rheidae, Apteryx) (4).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, crista deltopectoralis, angulus cristae (if present) or homologous locus, situs (unordered)  : proximal (0);  dorsal (1);  distal (2);  cranial, perpendicular to crista propria (3).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, crista deltopectoralis, impressio aut tuberculum insertii m. pectoralis (partes sternobrachialis et costobrachialis), status et forma (unordered)  : present, deep, elongate, elliptical depressio, or elevated, crescentic or ovate impressio (0);  present, modest tuberculum (1);  present, essentially sessile linea muscularis (2);  absent or indiscernable (3);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) (4).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, fossa pneumotricipitalis, foramen pneumaticum primus (new term), status (ordered)  : absent (0);  rudimentary or vestigial (1);  present, shallow, evidently related to sub- aquatic habit (2);  present, deep, (variably) significant (3);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) (4).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, fossa pneumotricipitalis (partes dorsalis et ventralis), status et forma pneumatica vis-Ã -vis fenestrae pneumaticae et pori pneumatici (unordered)  : absent, fossa apneumatic (0);  present, fossa pneumatic, pneumaticity rudimentary, effected by pori pneumatici perforating largely occlusive lamina osseum (1);  present, fossa moderately pneumatic, effected by fenestra pneumatica prima (orientation principally proximodorsad) et pori pneumatici (2);  present, fossa pneumatic, pneumaticity moderate, effected by fenestra pneumatica accessoria (orientation principally dorsodistad) et pori pneumatici (3);  present, fossa pneumatic, pneumaticity great, effected by fenestra pneumatica prima (orientation principally proximodorsad), fenestra pneumatica accessoria (orientation principally dorsodistad), et pori pneumatici (4);  present, fossa doubly pneumatic, pneumaticity extreme, effected by both fenestrae prima et accessoria in fossa pneumotricipitalis pars ventralis, et fenestra pneumatica in fossa pneumotricipitalis pars dorsalis (5);  noncomparable by absence of entire element (Dinornithiformes) or fossa (Dromaiidae, Apteryx, Dromornithidae) (6).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, facies caudalis, fossa pneumotricipitalis, subdivision by impressio origii m. humerotriceps, caput dorsale, to delimit pars ventralis fossae (new term)---virtually universal among Aves---et pars dorsalis fossae (new term)--- rarely pneumatic and of restricted expanse---status et forma (unordered)  : absent, fossa unipartite, comprising only homologue of pars ventralis fossae (0);  rudimentary, fossa comprising pars ventralis et pars dorsalis incipiens, latter typified by rudimentary crus proximale (juxtaposed with margo distalis capitis), but lacking distinct, distal sulcus or delimiting margines dorsalis et ventralis (1);  partial, fossa comprising pars ventralis et pars dorsalis incompletus, latter typified by distinct crus proximale (juxtaposed with margo distalis capitis) and shallow, abbreviated distal sulcus (2);  present, fossa bipartite, comprising both partes ventralis et dorsalis, each well developed and typically of comparable size (3);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) or fossa (Dromaiidae, Apteryx, Dromornithidae) (4).

Extremitas proximalis humeri, facies (palmaris) cranialis, impressio m. coracobrachialis cranialis (emended term), forma (unordered)  : indistinct or vaguely delimited (0);  moderately deep, moderately delimited (typically margo ventralis), modally subtriangular and comparatively proximal, i.e., margo proximalis bordering sulcus ligamentosus transversus (1);  moderately to very deep, margines distinctly elliptical, typically opposite in entirety crista deltopectoralis or proximal thereto (2);  very deep and delimited dorsally and ventrally by long, distinct cristulae, fossa elongate and triangular, joining perpendicularly with sulcus ligamentosa transversus (3);  noncomparable (ratites) (4).

Corpus humeri, departures from bilinearity by marginalis with respect to both plana dorsoventralis et craniocaudalis, forma (unordered)  : bi-linear---linear both craniocaudad et dorsoventrad (0);  dorsoventrally sigmoidal and craniocaudally linear---principally effected by ventral prominence of extremitas proximalis and dorsal prominence of extremitas distalis (1);  bi-sigmoidal---sigmoidal in both plana, craniocaudal component with extremitas proximalis caudad and extremitas distalis craniad (2);  dorsoventrally linear and craniocaudally sigmoid--- principally effected by caudal prominence of extremitas proximalis and cranial prominence of extremitas distalis (3);  dorsoventrally curvilinear, craniocaudally linear--- margo dorsalis linear and margo ventralis concave (4);  dorsoventrally curvilinear, craniocaudally sigmoidal--- margo dorsalis linear and margo ventralis concave (5);  moderately curvilinear craniocaudally---facies caudalis concave et facies cranialis convex (6);  moderately curvilinear craniocaudally---facies caudalis convex et facies cranialis concave (7);  strongly curvilinear or semilunate craniocaudally--- facies caudalis concave et facies cranialis convex (8);  curvilinear dorsoventrally, sigmoid craniocaudally--- margo dorsalis convex (9);  noncomparable (Aepyornis, Dinornithiformes, Sphenisciformes) (10).

Corpus humeri, facies caudalis, margo caudalis, angulus caudalis corporis (new term), proximodistal extent and proximal orientation, status et forma (unordered)  : absent essentially throughout (0);  present, distinctly angular and prominent throughout variably extensive portion of corpus humeri, proximally directed toward caput humeri (1);  present, variably distinct distally but proximally directed toward tuberculum ventrale (2);  present, distinct throughout majority of corpus humeri, proximally directed toward incisura capitis (3);  present, distinctly angular and prominent throughout variably extensive portion of corpus humeri, proximally directed toward tuberculum dorsale (4);  noncomparable (ratites, Dromornithidae, Alcidae, Strigidae) (5).

Extremitas distalis humeri, facies cranialis, incisura intercondylaris, lamina mediana sulci (new term) serving as boundary for sulcus ligamenti m. scapulotriceps, status et magnitudo (ordered)  : absent (0);  present, small (1);  present, moderate (2);  present, large (3);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) (4).

Extremitas distalis humeri, facies cranialis, fossa m. brachialis, status et forma sensu depth (ordered)  : absent (0);  present, rudimentary or vestigial (1);  present, moderately limited (2);  present, deep, typically including recessus ventralis fossae (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes) (4).

Extremitas distalis humeri, tuberculum (processus) supracondylaris dorsalis (as distinct from epicondylus dorsalis), status et forma (ordered)  : present, very prominent (exceeding dorsad extremitas distalis), subrectangular processus oriented dorsad (0);  present, prominent (exceeding dorsad extremitas distalis), subtriangular processus oriented dorsoproximad (1);  present, moderately large (approximating dorsad extremitas distalis), tuberculum (2);  present, small (exceeded dorsad by extremitas distalis), jugum or torus (3);  absent (4);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) (5).

Extremitas distalis humeri, tuberculum (processus) supracondylaris dorsalis, ancora origii m. extensor (meta)carpi radialis (or nonavian homologue), status, situs, et forma (unordered)  : absent or indiscernable (0);  distal, united, typically as impressio aut fovea on epicondylus dorsalis (1);  distal, separated by sulcus, a distinct tuberculum of processus supracondylaris dorsalis (2);  proximal, on conspicuous, subrectangular pro cessus on margo dorsalis corporis closely distal to crista deltopectoralis (3);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) (4).

Extremitas distalis humeri, processus flexorius (caudal perspective), status et forma (ordered)  : absent or indiscernable as distinct processus, although homologous situs typically indicated by impressio (angulus) tendinis origii (fossa muscularis) m. flexor (meta)carpi ulnaris (0);  present, limited to proximally restricted jugum (1);  present, moderately prominent, equaling complement of extremitas distalis distocaudally (2);  present, conspicuous, exceeding complement of extremitas distalis distocaudally (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes) (4).

Extremitas distalis humeri, tuberculum supracondylare ventrale, status et forma (unordered)  : absent or indiscernible (0);  present, sessile, comparatively truncate aspectus ancorae or weakly developed, proximally truncate eminentia, depressed and subparallel to facies cranialis of corpus humeri (1);  present, (sub)sessile, comparatively elongate (typically distinctly defined, ovate) aspectus ancorae, depressed and subparallel to facies cranialis of corpus humeri (2);  present, well-developed tuberculum, distal fovea angled distally and elevated, basal structure proximally extensive (3);  present, prominent processus distinctly proximal to epicondylus ventralis (4);  present, trenchant tuberculum well proximal to epicondylus ventralis (5);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes, Sphenisciformes) (6).

Extremitas distalis humeri, facies caudalis, fossa olecrani, status et forma (ordered)  : absent or obsolete, rudimentum aut vestigium (0);  present, limited depth and proximodistal width (1);  present, markedly deep, proximodistally broad, and (typically) sharply delimited (2);  present, extremely deep cavitas (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes) (4).

Os ulna, status et forma generalis (ordered)  : present, of typical prominence and structural detail (0);  present, moderate in relative length but retaining majority of structural details (1);  present, truncate in relative length and many structural details, especially of extremitates proximalis et distalis or simplified to subcylindrical vestigium in which extremitas distalis is synostotic with that of radius and ossa proximalia carpi (2);  present, vestigium broadly synostotic with other ossa antebrachii et manus or reduced to mere angularity (3);  absent (4).

Extremitas proximalis ulnae, ancora insertii m. scapulotricipitis, forma (unordered)  : impressio (infrequently barely discernable) or slightly elevated cristula or jugum (0);  facies ancorae subplanaris aut depressio subfovealis, of intermediate proximity to cotylae (1);  fovea, distinct and adjacent to rima cotylae dorsalis (2);  tuberculum, small but elevated (3);  torus, variably broad, suborbiculate, convex (4);  noncomparable (Sphenisciformes) (5).

Extremitas proximalis ulnae, olecranon, especially as related to impressio (tuberculum) insertii m. humerotriceps (proximally) et/aut impressio (fovea) trochlearis humeroulnaris (ventrally), status et forma (unordered)  : indiscernable, or an impressio not effecting distinct angular departure (0);  olecranon truncated, disproportionately blunted, in some taxa evidently replaced at least in part by ossa sesamoidea (1);  variably blunt angulus or tuberositas offset from olecranon (tuberculum insertii m. humerotriceps), and/or ventral subfoveate impressio (trochlea humeroulnaris) creating appearance of hamulation (2);  subtriangular tuberculum, aligned with olecranon proprius but distinguished by caudal prominence or proximal extension, typically acuminate (3);  noncomparable (ratites, Sphenisciformes, Raphidae) (4).

Corpus ulnae, papillae remigales caudales dorsales (caudales), status et forma (ordered)  : absent or indiscernable (0);  present, small impressiones or tumula (1);  present, substantial tuberositates (2);  present, prominent tuberculae (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes) (4).

Extremitas distalis ulnae, depressio radialis, status et forma (unordered)  : absent or indiscernable, regio sometimes convex (0);  present, shallow and nondescript (1);  present, moderately deep, distinctly triangular (2);  present, deep, foveate apneumatica (3);  present, deep, ovoid fossula pneumatica (4);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Dromornithidae) (5).

Extremitas distalis ulnae, trochlea carpalis, condylus dorsalis ulnae, labrum condyli dorsalis (dorsal perspective), forma marginalis distale (unordered)  : essentially flat (0);  uniformly rounded (orbiculate) throughout, ap proximate midpoint of arcus aligned with axis majoris ulnae (1);  generally rounded but with margo distalis flattened, resulting in rounded subrectangular profile with distinct, rounded, subangular vertices cranialis et caudalis (2);  rounded throughout, but with distinct increase in slope caudally, placing intersection of axis majoris ulnae cranial to midpoint of arcus (3);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes, Sphenisciformes) (4).

Extremitas distalis ulnae, tuberculum car- pale, status et forma sensu cranial prominence (ordered)  : absent, i.e., no extension beyond margo cranialis (0);  present, small, i.e., tuberculum appearing as mere angulus of extremitas distalis ulnae (1);  present, moderately large, i.e., tuberculum distinct but significantly less prominent than width of corpus caudal to tuberculum (2);  present, very prominent, i.e., tuberculum distinct, at least as prominent as width of corpus caudal to tuberculum (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Dromornithidae) (4).

Extremitas distalis ulnae, tuberculum car- pale, status et forma apicalis (unordered)  : cuneate, proximodistally wide, dorsoventrally thick (0);  blunt, unilobate, but some taxa with irregular facetae et tuberositates terminales (1);  bifurcate (2);  crescentiform (3);  noncomparable (ratites, Sphenisciformes, Pelecanidae, Aptornis) (4).

Extremitas proximalis radii, facies ventralis, tuberculum bicipitale radii, status et forma (unordered)  : absent (0);  present, a modest boss or tuberculum, essentially sessile on corpus (1);  present, a prominent, comparatively proximal tuberculum, including extreme position on margo cotylae (2);  present, impressio on prominent jugum (3);  present, an elevated, foveate processus or tuba (4);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) (5).

Extremitas distalis radii, facies ventralis, tuberculum aponeurosis ventralis, forma (unordered)  : inconspicuous, rounded (0);  prominent, angular or hemispheroidal tumulus (1);  conspicuously developed, peglike processus (2);  carinate (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes) (4).

Extremitas distalis radii, facies dorsalis, tumulus rotundus (new term), forma (unordered)  : subplanar or shallowly rounded (0);  prominently, irregularly shaped and surfaced, elevated regio (1);  distinctly delimited, comparatively low, triangular area (2);  significantly elevated, rounded, subtrianguloid (3);  cristulate (4);  noncomparable (ratites, Sphenisciformes, Pezophaps) (5).

Os carpi ulnare, corpus (craniocaudal perspective), forma (unordered)  : orbiculate to subrectangular (0);  cordiform (1);  parabolic (``U-shaped'') with deep incisura dorsocranialis carpi ulnaris (new term) delimiting two distinct crura (2);  equilaterally triangular, dorsoventrally compressed, sublaminate (3);  noncomparable (most ratites, Aptornis) (4).

Os metacarpale primus (I, alulare), status et typus (ordered)  : present, distinguishable, comparatively elongate, extending significantly distad to symphysis intermetacarpalis proximalis (0);  present, distinguishable, comparatively truncate, extending no farther distad than symphysis intermetacarpalis proximalis (1);  present, diminutive, synostotic with os metacarpale II (margo cranialis) et phalanx proximalis digiti I (2);  present, vestigial (3);  absent (4);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) (5).

Os metacarpale minus (III, tertius), corpus metacarpale, facies caudalis, sectiones proximalis et intermedius, forma superficialis (ordered)  : (sub)cylindrical (0);  (sub)laminar, flat (1);  slightly to moderately concave proximally (2);  deeply concave, forming conspicuous, longitudinal sulcus (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Sphenisciformes, Aptornis) (4).

Os metacarpale majus (II, secundus), comparative dorsoventral position of facies dorsalis and proximodistal alignment (caudal perspective) of element relative to that of os metacarpale minus (III, tertius), forma (unordered)  : proximodistally parallel, os metacarpale majus dorsoventrally equal to os metacarpale minus throughout (0);  proximodistally parallel, os metacarpale majus variably but notably dorsal to os metacarpale minus throughout (1);  proximodistally sloping ventrad, latter parallel or partially ventral to former at synostosis proximalis and uniting at vertex ventralis of synostosis distalis, in part related to narrowing of os metacarpale minus distad (2);  proximodistally parallel, os metacarpale majus almost completely dorsal to os metacarpale minus, latter ventral to former at synostosis proximalis, parallels margo ventralis of former to vertex ventralis at synostosis distalis, in some taxa associated wit (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornis, Dinornithiformes, Apteryx, Aptornis) (4).

Extremitas proximalis carpometacarpi, processus alularis, processus extensorius, length relative to craniocaudal width of trochlea carpalis including osseus basis calcarius (unordered)  : less, not part of calcar alae (0);  greater, calcar an osseus core for blunt calcar alae (1);  greater, calcar an osseus core for narrowly based, acuminate, keratin-covered calcar alae (2);  greater, calcar an osseus core for broadly based, acuminate, keratin-covered calcar alae (3);  equal or greater, calcar an irregular, variable, subspherical, multituberculate, often enormous lo- bus calcarius, covered by keratinized integumentum in life (4);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes) (5).

Extremitas proximalis carpometacarpi (new term), trochlea carpalis, relative proximal extents (craniocaudal perspective) of rima dorsalis (externum) et rima ventralis (internum) (ordered)  : former conspicuously greater than latter, defining approximately diagonal angulus (0);  former significantly greater than latter (1);  former slightly greater than or subequal to latter (2);  former equal to latter (3);  noncomparable, ossa alae or carpometacarpus proprius lacking (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Apteryx, Dromornithidae) (4).

Extremitas proximalis carpometacarpi, trochlea carpalis, facies dorsalis, facies articularis ulnocarpalis, rima dorsalis trochlearis, terminus distalis (caudal perspective), forma (unordered)  : essentially undistinguished, including modest irregularities or uniform conformation in parallel to rima ventralis (0);  marked by modest tumulus, apparently result of subterminal incisura and remnant of rima isolated thereby (1);  marked by prominent intumescentia (2);  marked by apparent terminal incisura or truncation, reflecting limited amelioration of embryonic inequality between ossa carpalia distalia---i.e., geometry of ``os scapholunare'' (proximal trochlea) and os giving rise to distal facies articularis ulnocarpa (3);  marked by apparent terminal incisura or truncation, reflecting virtual absence of modification of embryonic inequality between ossa carpalia distalia (4);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes, Dromaiidae, Casuariidae, Apteryx, Aptornis) (5).

Extremitas proximalis carpometacarpi, trochlea carpalis, facies ventralis, facies articularis ulnocarpalis (caudal perspective), terminus distalis, forma (unordered)  : essentially undistinguished from rest of rima (0);  modest tumulus, apparently result of subterminal incisura and remnant of rima isolated thereby (1);  prominent intumescentia (2);  caudally prominent arcus including discernable terminus at approximate mid planum of fovea caudalis (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Dromaiidae, Casuariidae, Apteryx, Aptornis) (4).

Extremitas proximalis carpometacarpi, trochlea carpalis, rima dorsalis (dorsal perspective), apex proximalis of rima dorsalis trochlearis (new term), forma (unordered)  : transversely flat (0);  broad, stout, and rounded (1);  narrow, elongate, and terminally rounded (2);  distinctly angular, subacuminate, elongated proximally (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Dromornithidae) (4).

Corpus carpometacarpi, os metacarpale ma- jus (II), facies cranioventralis, impressio proprius m. abductor digiti majoris (new term), status et forma (ordered)  : absent, corpus subcylindrical or subangular (0);  present, moderately deep and limited to distal half (1);  present, moderately or conspicuously deep, associated with planar facies ventralis corpus extend ing to margo distalis of basis ossis metacarpale alulae and to extremitas distalis carpometacarpi (2);  present, conspicuously deep, extends proximad to basis ossis metacarpale alulae or between processi extensorius et pisiformis and to extremitas distalis carpometacarpi (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Dromaiidae, Casuariidae, Apteryx, Dromornithidae, Aptornis) (4).

Corpus carpometacarpi, os metacarpale minus, margo caudalis, sulcus (impressio) origii m. flexor digiti minoris (new term), status et forma (ordered)  : absent (0);  present, principally limited to proximal half of corpus (1);  present, extending entire length of corpus (2);  present, extending entire length of corpus, augmented by distal lamella marginis (3).

Corpus carpometacarpi, spatium intermetacarpale (dorsoventral perspective), status et forma (ordered)  : absent, spatium precluded by proximodistally complete synostosis intermetacarpalis (0);  present, terminating proximad to terminus distalis of os metacarpale I (1);  present, extending distad to terminus distalis of os metacarpale I but proximad to extremitates ossa metacarpalia II et III (2);  present, extending distad to terminus distalis of os metacarpale II (3);  secondarily absent, diagnosable by profound truncation of manus (e.g., corollary of flightlessness) and/or secondary longitudinal synostosis between ossa metacarpalia majus et minus (4);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes) (5).

Corpus carpometacarpi, spatium intermetacarpale (if present), processus (lamina) intermetacarpalis extending caudad to facies dorsalis ossis metacarpale (III) minus to largely occlude proximal portion of spatium intermetacarpale (pons intermetacarpalis; new term), resulting in distinct disparity in size between ostia dorsalis (smaller) et ventralis (larger) of spatium, status et forma (unordered)  : absent (0);  present, occlusion comparatively narrow, processus essentially unrefined and retaining form despite junctura metacarpale (1);  present, occlusion comparatively broad, processus laminar, accommodating fenestra proximalis symphysis (new term) between margo proximalis pontis et symphysis metacarpalis proximalis (2);  present, occlusion comparatively broad, processus laminar, unfenestrated proximally (3);  noncomparable (Sphenisciformes) (4).

Phalanges digiti I (alularis, primus) manus, numerus modalis et forma (unordered)  : two, including functional phalanx ungualis, of uniform robustness (0);  two, in which phalanx ungualis reduced, largely nonfunctional, of uniform robustness (1);  two, including phalanx ungualis, latter typically vestigia (2);  present, robust and proximally hamulate, phalanges two in number, phalanx distalis sine unguis (3);  one, phalanx vestigialis, phalanx ungualis lacking (4);  zero, phalanges alulae lacking entirely (5);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes) (6).

Phalanges digiti II (majus, secundus) manus, numerus modalis et forma (ordered)  : three, phalanges of uniform (functional) robustness, including functional phalanx ungualis (0);  three, phalanges (including unguis) of comparable functionality as indicated by robustness of elements, phalanx distalis typically cum unguis (1);  three, phalanges typically decreasing in functionality and robustness progressively distad, phalanx distalis vestigial in Neornithes (2);  two, phalanges of uniform (functional) robustness, phalanx terminalis possessing unguis vestigialis (3);  two, phalanges of uniform (functional) robustness, phalanx terminalis lacking unguis (4);  one, phalanx cum ungualis (5);  zero, digitus II (majoris) lacking entirely (6);  noncomparable, ossa alae absent or synostotic (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes) (7).

Phalanges digiti minus (III, tertius), numerus modalis (ordered)  : four, proximalis typically shortest among included Avialae (0);  three (1);  two (2);  one (3);  zero, despite retention of os metacarpale III, typically vestigial (4);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Aptornis) (5).

Phalanx proximalis digiti II (majus, secundus) manus, margo caudalis phalangis (new term), orientation of axis marginis caudalis phalangis relative to axis marginis cranialis phalangis (new term), forma (unordered)  : shallowly concave or linear (0);  slightly convex (1);  angular, proximodistally divergent (2);  moderately or strongly convex (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Dromaiidae, Casuariidae, Apteryx, Aptornis) (4).

Phalanx proximalis digiti II (majus, secundus) manus, corpus phalangis, fossa dorsalis phalan gis, translucentia(e) aut fenestra(e) ovalis(es) (new term), status, typus et numerus (ordered)  : absent or obsolete (0);  present, single or (more frequently) paired, clearly emarginated translucentia ovales phalangis (1);  present, singular, pars caudodistalis fossae dorsalis phalangis, essentially circular, typically positioned in articulatio (dorsal perspective) between tendines insertii mm. interossea dorsalis et ventralis (2);  present, paired fenestrae, pars caudodistalis fossae dorsalis phalangis, separated by pila obliqua fossae (3);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Dromaiidae, Casuariidae, Apteryx, Dromornithidae, Aptornis) (4).

Juncturae cubiti, trochlea humero-ulnaris--- partes humeralis proprius et accessoria ulnaris (new terms)---variation associated with mm. expansor secundariorum et flexor (meta)carpi ulnaris, status et typus (unordered)  : trochlea absent, or if present, comprising only pars ulnaris as origo m. expansor secundariorum, m. flexor (meta)carpi ulnaris reduced to tendo (0);  trochlea present, comprising partes humeralis proprius, humeralis accessoria, et ulnaris (1);  trochlea present, comprising partes humeralis proprius et ulnaris, associated with reduction of m. expansor secundariorum to tendo (2);  trochlea present, comprising partes humeralis proprius, humeralis accessoria, et ulnaris, but origo tendinis m. expansor secundariorum comparatively caudodistal and, together with pars ulnaris, guides tendo m. flexor (meta)carpi ulnaris, typically associa (3);  trochlea present, comprising only pars humeralis proprius (Hemiprocne comata), humeralis accessoria (Cypseloides niger, Apus pallidus), aut ulnaris, the last united with a neomorphous fascia ligamentosa cum sesamoideum origii m. extensor metacarpi ulnaris (4);  noncomparable (Dinornithiformes, Dromornithidae) (5).

Synchon-synostoses intermetacarpales (new term), especially spatium intermetacarpale, status et typus (unordered)  : absent, synostoses intermetacarpalia lacking (0);  partial, synostosis intermetacarpalis proximalis lacking or incomplete, but synostosis intermetacarpalis distalis complete (1);  partial, synostosis intermetacarpalis proximalis complete, synostosis intermetacarpalis distalis incomplete in that sutura remains discernable, region having aspect of deep fissura (2);  partial, synostosis intermetacarpalis proximalis present but synostosis intermetacarpalis distalis lacking, ossa metacarpalia II et III separate distally (3);  present, comprising ossa metacarpale alulare, metacarpale majus, and metacarpale minus, with synostoses intermetacarpales proximalis et distalis complete, enclosing spatium intermetacarpale (4);  vestigial, ossa metacarpale majus et minus truncated distally, synostosis metacarpalis distalis and extremitas distalis carpometacarpi present and occluding spatium entirely (5);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes) (6).

Spatium ischiopubica (lateral perspective), status et forma (unordered)  : wide (divergent) incisura---delimited by widely divergent ala postacetabulares alae ischii et pubici (0);  intermediate incisura---by absence of caudal completion of membrana ischiopubica ossificans, craniocaudally of moderately deep, subuniform width (1);  narrow incisura---by absence of caudal completion of membrana ischiopubica ossificans, of narrow shape with subparallel margines (2);  wide fenestra---by presence of membrana ischiopubica ossificans, dorsoventrally deep, semi- ellipsoidal in shape (3);  narrow fenestra---by presence of membrana ischiopubica ossificans, dorsoventrally narrow with subparallel margines dorsalis et ventralis or triangular outline, and terminated comparatively craniad on ala ischii (4);  absent---replaced by synchondrosis ischiopubica by variable combination of membrana ischiopubica ossificans and proximity of ischium et pubis (5).

Foramen ilioischiadicum (if caudally delimited), forma definitiva (ordered)  : ``ellipsoidal-planar''---with pronounced axis majoris craniocaudad in orientation (0);  ``subcircular-planar'' or orbiculate---with weakly defined axis majoris (if discernable) craniocaudad in orientation (1);  ``subcircular-caudodorsal''---with variably pronounced axis majoris having cranial terminus distinctly dorsal to caudal terminus (2);  ``subcircular-caudoventral''---with variably pronounced axis majoris having cranial terminus distinctly ventral to caudal terminus (3);  noncomparable by absence of delimiting membrana ilioischiadica ossificans (nonavialian Therapoda, palaeognathous Neornithes) (4).

Fossa renalis, recessus caudalis fossae (if present), depth as reflected by number of vertebrae caudales stabiles interposed between bilateral recessi and distinctly differentiated (e.g., thickened, ventrally displaced crista caudalis fossae renalis) as medial supports for lamina ventralis of same, numerus vertebralia (ordered)  : zero (0);  one (1);  two (2);  three (3);  noncomparable where recessus absent (4).

Fossa renalis, recessus caudalis fossae, craniocaudal length of internum (margo cranialis of which is crista caudalis fossae renalis) relative to craniocaudal width of lamina infracristalis, status et forma (ordered)  : absent, sensu lacking measurable internum (0);  present, depth of recessus comparatively shallow, craniocaudal internal depth less than one-fourth of craniocaudal width of lamina infracristalis (1);  present, depth of recessus comparatively moderate, craniocaudal internal depth between one- fourth and one-half of craniocaudal width of lamina infracristalis (2);  present, depth of recessus comparatively great, craniocaudal internal depth greater than one-half of craniocaudal width of lamina infracristalis (3).

Ala (pars) preacetabularis ilii, facies dorsalis, margo cranialis et crista lateralis, processus craniolateralis (new term), or vertex of margo cranialis et margo lateralis of ala (pars) preacetabularis ilii, forma (unordered)  : rounded or straight (0);  strongly curved (1);  acuminate (2);  elongated, laterally prominent, abrupt, angular flange (3);  dorsocaudally oriented, tuberculate eminentia (4).

Pars acetabularis ilii, interacetabular width relative to synsacral length, magnitudo (ordered)  : great, exceeds one-half synsacral length (0);  moderate, one-half to one-third synsacral length (1);  small, approximately one-fourth synsacral length (2);  extremely small, approximately one-sixth synsacral length (3).

Pars acetabularis et ala postacetabularis ilii, facies ventralis, crista iliaca obliqua, caudal distinctness relative to (i) acetabulum, (ii) recessus caudalis fossae, et (iii) crista caudalis fossae renalis, forma (ordered)  : crista iliaca obliqua remaining strongly differentiated caudad to medial inflection to sutura iliosynsacralis, effectively continuous with crista caudalis fossae renalis (0);  crista iliaca obliqua becoming indistinct cranial to recessus caudalis fossae or margo foraminis ilioischiadica caudalis, typically appearing to continue caudad as pila ischiadica (1);  crista iliaca obliqua becoming indistinct opposite or immediately caudal to acetabulum (2);  crista iliaca obliqua absent or obsolete throughout (3);  noncomparable (palaeognathous Neornithes) (4).

Ala (pars) postacetabularis ilii, facies dorsalis, spina dorsolateralis ilii, caudal extent relative to that of ala ischii, processus terminalis ischii, forma (ordered)  : former greater than latter (0);  former subequal to latter (1);  former distinctly but not substantially shorter than latter (2);  former substantially shorter than latter, difference approximately shorter than latter by twice the craniocaudal depth of the incisura marginis caudalis (3).

Ala (pars) postacetabularis ilii, facies lateralis (lateral perspective), lamina infracristalis ilii, margo foraminis ilioischiadici (exclusive of vestigia of membrana ossificans ilioischiadica, if present), status et forma (unordered)  : absent, lamina infracristalis lacking (0);  present, delimiting a subangular, significantly caudally attenuated margo (1);  present, delimiting a shallow (axis minoris less than one-half axis majoris) elliptical to circular margo (2);  present, delimiting a deep (axis minoris at least one-half axis majoris) elliptical to circular margo (3).

Alae (partes) preacetabulares et postacetabulares ilii, facies dorsalis, cristae iliacae dorsolaterales, vertex craniomedialis cristae (new term) relative to axis transacetabularis, situs craniocaudalis (unordered)  : ``hypercranial,'' such that cristae extend without intersection with margo cranialis of ala preacetabularis ilii (0);  moderately cranial (1);  approximately equal (2);  distinctly caudal (3);  noncomparable (Apteryx) (4).

Ala ischii, sulcus obturatorius, prominence as reflected by craniocaudal extent, distinctness, and laterodorsal support by membrana ossificans attached to margo ventralis of ala ischii, forma (ordered)  : obsolete, spatium for musculus concerned provided by medially convex ischium et laterally convex pubis (0);  discernable but limited in structural delimitation (1);  distinctly, but not exceptionally manifested (2);  conspicuously determinate of margo ventralis ischii, effecting either a demarcated laminar surface or deep sulcus laterally augmented by comparatively extensive membrana ischiopubica ossificans (3).

Scapus (corpus) pubis, exclusive of marked departures in apex pubis (lateral perspective), margo dorsalis, forma dorsoventralis (unordered)  : decurved, margo dorsalis convex (0);  essentially straight or sigmoid (latter typically recurved craniad and decurved caudad), approximately aligned with axis majoris of apex pubis (1);  slightly but distinctly recurved, margo dorsalis moderately concave (2);  conspicuously recurved, margo dorsalis deeply concave (3).

Scapus (corpus) pubis (dorsal perspective), pars intermedia (i.e., between tuberculum obturatorius cranially and processus terminalis ischii caudally), facies lateralis, forma lateromedialis (ordered)  : concave (0);  straight (1);  slightly to moderately convex laterally (2);  strongly convex laterally, apices typically closely approaching or contacting caudomedially (3).

Apex pubis, facies lateralis (lateral perspective), dorsoventral components of axis majoris apicalis (new term) relative to axis craniocaudalis synsacralis, forma dorsoventralis (ordered)  : caudal (0);  caudoventral (1);  ventral (2);  caudodorsal (3).

Junctura ischiopubica (caudalis) distalis, status et typus (unordered)  : absent (0);  variable (craniocaudally abbreviated) synchondrosis, often of limited robustness and permitting separation of elements during preparation, or (if distinguishable) articulatio (1);  substantial synchondrosis distalis, forming a dorsoventrally deep lamina (2);  variably extensive and oriented sutura distalis (3).

Synchondrosis ischiopubica caudalis, status et forma (ordered)  : absent, juncturae ischiopubica limited to synostosis within rima acetabularis (0);  present, incomplete, limited to or including synchondroses ischiopubicae medio-apicales (new term), i.e., those involving the apices pubici (1);  present, moderately and variably complete and robust synchondrosis between ischia (margo ventralis) et apex pubis (2);  present, complete, essentially joining ischia (margo ventralis) with os pubis (margo dorsalis) through majority of elements where in dorsoventral opposition, either cranially or caudally (3).

Symphysis pubica medio-apicalis (new term), caudomedial proximity, status et forma (ordered)  : absent (0);  present, moderate caudomedial proximity, ankylosis absent (1);  present, caudomedial proximity pronounced, ankylosis absent (2);  present, extreme, ankylosis present, producing symphysis pubica medio-apicalis (new term) (3).

Extremitas distalis femoris, condylus lateralis, crista tibiofibularis, terminus proximalis on facies cranialis corporis, forma superficialis (unordered)  : strongly convex, prominent well cranial to facies cranialis corporis (0);  moderately convex (1);  sublinear (2);  concave, especially at proximal extreme (3);  poorly defined, tumulate (4).

Extremitas distalis femoris, condylae lateralis et medialis, facies cranialis, extremitates proximales condylarum, condylus lateralis relative to that of condylus medialis, proximal extent (ordered)  : lateral exceptionally proximal (0);  lateral moderately proximal (1);  lateral of subequal proximity (2);  lateral moderately distal (3).

Patella, facies (distalis) cranialis, forma generalis (unordered)  : nondescript or weakly demarcated (0);  bilobate---distinct tumulus or jugum (1);  cristate---marked dorsoventrally oriented crista partitioning approximately equal depressiones lateralis et medialis (2);  cuneate---prominent, elongate, broadly based eminentia aligned with axis majoris tibiotarsi (3);  angular---extremely prominent, elongate, acute eminentia aligned with axis majoris tibiotarsi (4);  noncomparable by absence of patella (Tinamidae, Puffinus, Pelecanoides, Heliornithidae, Rostratula) (5).

Extremitas proximalis tibiotarsi, caput tibiotarsi, cristae cnemiales cranialis et lateralis, crista cnemialis lateralis, margo dorsalis cristae, laterad to intersectio with crista cnemialis cranialis, forma marginalis (unordered)  : concave essentially throughout (0);  sigmoidal, convex laterally and concave medially (1);  linear and variably sloping throughout (2);  convex essentially throughout (3).

Extremitas proximalis tibiotarsi, caput tibiotarsi, sulcus (intercnemialis) intercristalis cnemialis, pori superficiae (new term) cristae (internal or external to sulcus), status et forma (unordered)  : absent, facies internae sulci essentially smooth, imperforate (0);  present, facies sulci with pori pneumatici, nutrientes, et/aut neurovasculariae (1);  present, facies sulci with typically suborbiculate foramina pneumatica (2);  present, facies sulci conspicuously sculpted with multilayered, overlapping, irregularly shaped, spiculae tubiformes et marginally rounded fenestrae (3).

Extremitas proximalis tibiotarsi, caput tibiotarsi, crista cnemialis cranialis, facies lateralis cristae, forma (ordered)  : essentially planar (0);  only slightly concave, as lateroproximal jugum, or obsolete, strictly proximodistally oriented jugum (1);  moderately, typically heterogeneously concave, pronounced proximally (2);  deep, elongate, distally diminished sulcus (3).

Extremitas proximalis tibiotarsi, caput tibiotarsi, crista cnemialis cranialis, margo cranialis cristae (lateromedial perspective), forma (unordered)  : parallel sublinear---cranioproximal prominence lacking (0);  sloping sublinear---sublinear slope from proximocranial angulus to facies cranialis corporis (1);  shallow subangular---suborbiculate dorsad, distinct intermediate angulus, sublinear junctura with corpus distad (2);  deep subangular or suborbiculate (3).

Extremitas proximalis tibiotarsi, caput tibiotarsi, crista cnemialis lateralis, crista patellaris, forma (unordered)  : variable with respect to thickness and angularity, margo ventralis cristae approximately diagonal with respect to margo lateralis tibiotarsi (0);  subtubercular (1);  thick, blunt, hamulate, or strongly angular (2);  thin, acuminate, very prominent laterally, and hamulate (3);  prominent and crescentiform, imbedded within vertex lateroproximalis of cristae cnemiales, subperpendicular to margo lateralis tibiotarsi (4);  truncate and crescentiform, imbedded within vertex lateroproximalis of unified cristae cnemiales, at obtuse angulus with corpus tibiotarsi (5).

Corpus tibiotarsi, crista fibularis, margo lateralis cristae (craniocaudal perspective), forma marginalis (unordered)  : essentially linear, i.e., crista of approximately uniform breadth (0);  distally deepening, i.e., crista distinctly broadest distally, least broad proximally (1);  concave, i.e., sectio intermedius cristae of minimal lateral breadth (2);  convex, i.e., sectio intermedius cristae of maximal lateral breadth (3);  distally diminishing, i.e., crista distinctly broadest proximally, least broad distally (4);  noncomparable (Aepyornithiformes, Dinornithiformes, Phaethon, Turnix) (5).

Corpus tibiotarsi, margo lateralis (fibularis), foramen interosseum distale, status et forma sensu length relative to that of foramen interosseum proximale (unordered)  : absent, spina fibulae terminating or effectively free-standing at crista fibularis, thereby failing to define foramen interosseum distale (0);  present, essentially occluded by proximity to tibiotarsus et septum interosseum, distinctly shorter than foramen interosseum distale (1);  present, moderately elongate, subequal to foramen interosseum proximale (2);  present, elongate, significantly longer than foramen interosseum proximale (3).

Corpus tibiotarsi, linea extensoria, tuberositas proximalis retinaculi mm. extensorum, status et forma (unordered)  : present, modestly elevated jugum, eminentia, aut tuberculum (0);  present, sessile impressio (1);  absent (2);  present, prominent cristulate processus (3).

Extremitas distalis tibiotarsi, condylus medialis, depressiones epicondylares medialis et lateralis, status (unordered)  : absent (0);  present, depressio medialis only (1);  present, depressio lateralis only (2);  present, both depressiones medialis et lateralis, typically demarcating condylae propriae from crista cartilagines (3).

Extremitas distalis tibiotarsi, depressiones condylorum medialis et lateralis, foveae ligamentosae (new term), status et forma (unordered)  : absent or indiscernable (0);  present, limited to fovea (incisura) medialis, typically dividing condylus proprius from crista sulci (1);  present, limited to fovea medialis, but uniquely conformed as sulcus obliquus condyli (new term) oriented proximolaterad to distomediad (2);  present, comprising both foveae medialis et lateralis (3).

Corpus fibulae, terminus spinae, situs proximodistalis (ordered)  : margines distales of ossa proximalia tarsi to articulate (independently) with ossa distalia tarsi within articulatio intertarsales (0);  margines proximales of ossa proximalia tarsi, typically terminus of os fibulare resting within fossa of os fibulare (1);  facies lateralis of (typically synostotic) ossa proximalia tarsi (typically within sulcus or lateral fovea between ossa tarsi proximales et os tibia propria aut condylus cartilaginis tibialis) but proximal to margines proximales of ossa proximalia tarsi (2);  less than entirety of tibiotarsus but at least three-fourths of tibiotarsus (3);  less than three-fourths but typically at least one-half of tibiotarsus (4);  less than one-half of tibiotarsus but at least one- fourth of tibiotarsus (5).

Os metatarsale I (primum), status modalis (unordered)  : present, typically robust, retaining phalanges proximalis et ungualis (0);  present, vestigial, truncated, lacking torsion and tuberositates poorly defined (1);  present, vestigial, with phalanx vestigial or absent (2);  absent, also lacking phalanges (3).

Os metatarsale I (primum), corpus metarsalis, forma generalis---(i) distinct reduction characterized by lateromedial and dorsoplantar narrowing, (ii) conformational change in which facies articularis tarsometatarsalis is subacuminate and distinctly narrower than trochlea, and (iii) morphoclinal reduction in general robustness (even presence) of os metatarsale I et digitus I---status (ordered)  : absent (0);  present, os metatarsale et both phalanges digiti I conserved and semifunctional, tuberositates medialis et lateralis trochlearis asymmetrical (1);  present, os metatarsale et both phalanges digiti I conserved but vestigial, only one tuberositas trochlearis moderately developed (2);  present, os metatarsale vestigial or absent, and digitus I obsolete or absent (3);  noncomparable in absence of element (4).

Extremitas proximalis tarsometatarsi, impressio (tuberositas) ligamentum collateralis lateralis, forma (unordered)  : impressio aut tuberositas, typically indistinct (0);  fossa aut fovea, craniodorsally angled on or proximate to rima dorsalis of cotyla lateralis (1);  tuberculum aut jugum, comparatively robust (2);  substantial fovea with prominent lateral laminar tuberculum (3).

Extremitas proximalis tarsometatarsi, facies dorsalis, fossa infracotylaris dorsalis, foramina vascularia proximalia (dorsal perspective), forma sensu situs, numerus modalis et forma (unordered)  : one distal, medial foramen (0);  two (micro)foramina comprising distal pair, both lateral to midline (1);  two foramina comprising distal, bilateral pair (2);  three foramina comprising (i) proximal, medial, single foramen, and (ii) distal, lateromedially (sub) parallel pair (3).

Hypotarsus (proximal perspective), dorsoplantar position with respect to corpus (ordered)  : entirely plantar to facies plantaris corporis, depth distinctly less than that of corpus (0);  entirely plantar to facies plantaris corporis, depth approximating that of corpus (1);  entirely plantar to facies plantaris corporis, depth at least as great as that of corpus, typically exceeding latter (2);  partly to largely dorsal to facies plantaris corporis, forming recessus hypotarsi corporis (3);  noncomparable by absence (palaeognathous Neornithes) (4).

Hypotarsus, canales et/aut sulci hypotarsi--- ``tendinal passage 1'' of Strauch (1978) or ``anteromedial canal'' of Stallcup (1954  : 6)---canalis tendinis insertii m. flexor digitorum longus (Vanden Berge and Storer 1995 (0);  8), status et forma modalis (unordered) (1);  absent, indiscernable or shallow sulcus (2);  present, deep, majority-delimited sulcus or canalis (3);  present, conjoined with tendinal passage 2 of Strauch (1978), i.e., with canalis tendinorum (i)m. flexor perforatus digiti IV et (ii) m. flexor perforans et perforatus digiti II (4);  present, conjoined with tendinal passage 3 of Strauch (1978), i.e., with canalis tendinis m. flexor hallucis longus (5);  noncomparable (palaeognathous Neornithes, Dromornithidae) (6).
